text:
Coucou

 A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows and Linux — and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. And now on your phone too: iPhone and Android. 

Approve permissions, watch your agents work, drop a file, chat with Claude — all without leaving what you're doing. Walk away from your Mac and Mochi follows you to your iPhone: Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, widgets, Siri.

 New in 0.4: Coucou is a real Mac app. Hold a key anywhere, speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, like Wispr Flow — free, open source, and offline with Parakeet. Record your calls without a bot in the meeting and get the transcript, the summary and the to-dos.

 

 New: Botan. Mochi is leaving the notch. Botan snaps onto the back of your iPhone. Join the founders list ↗ 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 

---

 Why

Some studios showed off gorgeous notch companions… and never let anyone use them.
 Coucou is the open version. Every line of code is open source under the MIT License: read it, fork it, learn from it. The Coucou name, Mochi and the sounds stay © Louis Raillé (see License).

Meet Mochi : a soft little squircle with big eyes that pops out of your notch, waves hello, follows your cursor with its eyes, gets annoyed when you poke it (and dizzy if you insist), and tells you the moment Claude Code needs you.

 Botan: Mochi in real life

 

Mochi is leaving the notch. Botan is my next project: it snaps onto the back of your iPhone, and I'm building it in public.

The founders list is open: join it to follow the build and hear everything first. Join the founders ↗ 

 Coucou on the Mac: dictation, notes, one window

 
 
 

Since 0.4, Coucou has its own window and sits in the Dock. On the left, Flow — everything about your voice — and Notch , all the settings of the island. (macOS, GitHub build) 

- 🎙️ Flow dictation — hold a key anywhere on the Mac (right ⌥ by default, or fn, right ⌘ or right ⌃), speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, in any app. Two quick taps for hands-free (or one, with a setting), Esc to cancel, ⌃⌘V to paste the last one again. Your clipboard gets back what it held.
- 💊 The pill — a small see-through pill at the bottom of the screen (or on its left or right edge). Hover it for a toolbar: dictate, record a call, open Coucou. While you speak, Mochi listens and nine dots follow your voice.
- 🦜 Parakeet, offline — run NVIDIA's Parakeet on your Mac's Neural Engine through FluidAudio: more accurate, 25 languages, nothing leaves your Mac. One click to download (about 650 MB), Apple silicon only. Until then the Mac's own recognition is used.
- ✍️ Your words, your way — a dictionary of names Coucou always spells right, replacements, snippets (say a short phrase, paste a whole text), and an optional clean-up by Claude, on your Claude plan through Claude Code or with your own key: as said, natural or polished, per app.
- 📝 Notetaker — click Record a call: Coucou records your microphone and what your Mac plays, no bot joins the call. Then you get the transcript person by person, a summary, the key points and the to-dos, written by Claude with your key or by Apple Intelligence on your Mac. The audio is deleted once the transcript is written. Tell the people in the call that you record.
- 📊 Statistics — words dictated, time saved, words per minute, days in a row and the apps you dictate in. Counted on your Mac, never sent anywhere.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Flow dictation and the Notetaker are on the Mac for now; Windows and Linux are next.

 Features

- 🤖 Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Muse Code, OpenCode, Amp, Hermes, Claude Desktop and other agents, live — see every session in your notch: what it reads, edits and runs, step by step. Tag a hook payload with coucou agent to give any agent its own pill (see docs/AGENTS.md ). Finished? Mochi does a happy little jump.
- See what Claude is editing, live in the notch: each file modification shows the file name and +N −M counts in the ticker, tap to read the full diff
- ✅ Approve and answer from the notch — Claude Code permission requests show up with Allow / Deny / Always ; AskUserQuestion prompts show the choices right in the notch (single or multi-select, up to 4 questions). One click, or "Reply in terminal" to fall back to the CLI. Codex also gets Allow / Deny.
- 🧑‍💻 Jump to the right terminal — open the exact terminal window of a session (macOS) .
- 💬 Chat with Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, or a local model (Ollama / LM Studio) — click the model name above the chat box to switch provider and pick a model. Cloud providers use your own API key; local providers connect to a server running on your Mac. No API key? Use your subscription : switch it on in Settings → Chat and the chat goes through the official terminal tool you already pay for, signed in with your own account — Claude Code, Antigravity CLI or Gemini CLI, Codex CLI (ChatGPT), Cursor CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI (GitHub build, Windows, Linux) . (Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot and local models: macOS) 
- 📈 Portfolio pill (macOS) — track your crypto across 16 networks (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, BNB, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Dogecoin, Litecoin, TRON, XRP, Cardano, Cosmos, NEAR) and 5 exchanges (Binance, OKX, Bybit, Kraken, Coinbase) in the notch. Live balances, 7-day sparklines and 24-hour price change per holding. Read-only API keys for exchanges, public addresses for wallets — nothing leaves your Mac.
- 📊 Claude plan usage (macOS, GitHub build) — a small pill in the notch header shows your 5-hour and weekly Claude plan limits. Enable it from Settings → Agents → Plan usage. Pro and Max plans only.
- 📊 Codex plan usage (macOS, GitHub build) — a Codex pill next to it shows your Codex limits and how many free resets you have left, read from the Codex CLI. Turn it on in Settings → Agents → Plan usage.
- 📋 Declare the tools you use — open Setti

install.title: Install
install.html:
App Store

Coucou is coming to the Mac App Store and the iPhone App Store: one click to install, automatic updates, and the iPhone app pairs with your Mac through your iCloud account, with nothing to configure. The links will be here as soon as Apple publishes them.

The App Store build of the Mac app runs in Apple's sandbox, so some features stay in the GitHub build: agents other than Claude Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop (Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI…), Claude and Codex plan usage, the chat through your AI subscription, the Coucou window (Flow dictation, the Notetaker, settings search), « OK Coucou », Mail, WhatsApp, Apple Music, Spotify, the Portfolio pill, screen capture, attaching the front window to the chat, and updates from inside the app (the App Store updates it).

iPhone
  1. Install Coucou on your iPhone (iOS 18 or later): install TestFlight from the App Store, then Join the TestFlight beta. The beta is free; Apple limits it to 10,000 testers. The App Store version is coming soon. Apple is reviewing the beta: it opens within a day or two — if the link isn't accepting testers yet, check back soon.
  2. On your Mac, with Coucou 0.1.9 or later: Settings… → General → iPhone, turn on Show my agent sessions on my iPhone, and Move Mochi to my iPhone's Dynamic Island when my Mac is locked for the Lock Screen.
  3. Same Apple Account in iCloud on the Mac and the iPhone. That's the whole link: no account, no pairing code.
  4. Open Coucou on the iPhone, allow notifications, and start a Claude Code session on the Mac.

Everything else, troubleshooting included, is in docs/IPHONE.md.

Android
  1. Download Coucou-Android-0.6.0.apk from the release page on your phone (Android 11 or later) and open it. Android asks once to allow installs from your browser or file manager. You can also build it from source.
  2. On your computer, install Coucou 0.4.0 or later for Windows or Linux: Settings → Android phone, turn on Phone link. If Windows asks about the firewall, allow Coucou on private networks.
  3. Show pairing code and scan it with the app. The phone and the computer must be on the same Wi-Fi.

Everything else, troubleshooting included, is in android/README.md.

Homebrew (macOS)
brew tap louis-cfm/coucou https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou
brew install --cask coucou

It installs the same signed and notarized GitHub build as the download below. Coucou then updates itself from the notch; brew upgrade --cask --greedy coucou works too.

Download for macOS
  1. Grab the latest Coucou.zip from Releases.
  2. Unzip and move Coucou.app to /Applications.
  3. Launch it, and click Open when macOS asks you to confirm. Updating from 0.1.0? macOS may ask you, once for each key you saved, to let Coucou use it: enter your Mac password and click Always Allow.
Windows

Download Coucou-Windows.msi or Coucou-Windows-setup.exe (Windows 10/11, always the newest version) and run it. You can also build it from source.

Windows will show a warning the first time — that's expected. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen doesn't know the publisher:

  1. A "Windows protected your PC" screen appears, with Publisher: Unknown publisher.
  2. Click More info (Informations complémentaires in French). This reveals a Run anyway button.
  3. Click Run anyway (Exécuter quand même). The installer starts normally.

This is only because the app isn't signed with a paid certificate yet. Coucou is open source, and Microsoft Defender scans the installer as clean.

Windows and Linux 0.6.0 start a Claude Code session from the island (pick a project, say what to do) or from Coucou for Android 0.6.0, drop a file on a session to put its path in the prompt, and approve Antigravity and OpenCode from the island. 0.5.9 keep a small island at the top of the screen once it is closed (Mochi, the time or your Claude usage in it), fold it with ✕, keep your language when you dictate, take any dictation key you like and, on Windows, quiet the other apps while you speak. 0.5.8 bring 14 fixes and features by @Ohualtex: permission requests wait their turn, Claude Desktop cards on Windows and its pill on Linux, plan usage in the compact island. 0.5.7 bring Mail to Windows with classic Outlook (search, automatic sorting, mail plans from the chat) and a search field for the settings. 0.5.6 chat on your own AI subscription (Claude Code, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Copilot) and speak Korean and Japanese. 0.5.5 answer on your Claude plan through Claude Code when no API key is saved. 0.5.4 bring 25 reliability fixes from the community. 0.5.3 bring WhatsApp to the island (experimental), with the gateway installed in one click. 0.5.2 turn Mochi blue when a new version waits and show what it brings after the update; they add GitLab and Gitea pills. 0.5.1 tell you when a new version is out (once you agree) and, on Windows, install it in one click; they also speak German and Turkish. 0.5.0 caught up with the Mac: Coucou is now an app with its own window in the taskbar, Flow dictation anywhere (hold right Ctrl, speak, let go) with Parakeet running offline on your computer, the Notetaker for your calls, and « OK Coucou » to talk to Mochi, powered by Claude with your key. On Linux, dictation works on X11 and Wayland. 0.4.0 paired with Coucou for Android: approve, answer and chat from your Android phone (Settings → Android phone, off by default). 0.3.0 added open on hover, your own sounds, a colour of your own for each Mochi and the Mochi-to-desktop shortcut; on Linux, the Spotify pill with Mochi dancing to it, global shortcuts on Wayland and "Open terminal" that brings the terminal forward. 0.2.0 caught up with the Mac: Codex, Copilot CLI, Muse Code and six more agents with approvals from the island, answers to Claude's questions, live diffs, GitHub pull requests and CI, plan usage, local models, the wardrobe, Mochi on the desktop, keyboard shortcuts, the weekly recap and 10 languages. See the changelog.

There is no notch on a PC, so the island slides out of the top edge of the screen instead of hiding inside one. See windows/README.md for the rest of the differences.

New versions. Once you agree (the island asks once, or Settings → General → Updates), Coucou for Windows and Linux tells you when a new version is out; on Windows, Update now downloads the installer you used, checks its SHA-256 against the one GitHub publishes and installs it in one click. See windows/README.md.

Linux

Coucou for Linux 0.6.0 is out (x86_64): AppImage · .deb · .rpm · all files and checksums. The newest AppImage is always at linux-latest.

  • AppImage (any distribution): chmod +x Coucou-Linux-*.AppImage, then run it.
  • Debian / Ubuntu: sudo apt install ./Coucou-Linux-*.deb
  • Fedora / openSUSE: sudo dnf install ./Coucou-Linux-*.rpm

Check a download with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing. On Arch Linux, build it with the PKGBUILD; on NixOS, use the flake.

The island sits on the top edge on compositors with layer-shell — COSMIC, KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Sway and other wlroots compositors. GNOME has no layer-shell, so there it runs through XWayland as a dock window at the top of the screen. See windows/README.md.

NixOS

Coucou has a Nix flake for x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux. It builds Coucou from source on your machine, so the first build takes a while (about 20 minutes on a laptop, mostly Rust).

Try it without installing anything:

nix run github:Louis-CFM/coucou

Flakes not turned on yet? Add --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' after nix.

features.title: Features
features.html:
• 🤖 Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Muse Code, OpenCode, Amp, Hermes, Claude Desktop and other agents, live — see every session in your notch: what it reads, edits and runs, step by step. Tag a hook payload with coucou_agent to give any agent its own pill (see docs/AGENTS.md). Finished? Mochi does a happy little jump.
  • See what Claude is editing, live in the notch: each file modification shows the file name and +N −M counts in the ticker, tap to read the full diff
  • ✅ Approve and answer from the notch — Claude Code permission requests show up with Allow / Deny / Always; AskUserQuestion prompts show the choices right in the notch (single or multi-select, up to 4 questions). One click, or "Reply in terminal" to fall back to the CLI. Codex also gets Allow / Deny.
  • 🧑‍💻 Jump to the right terminal — open the exact terminal window of a session (macOS).
  • 💬 Chat with Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, or a local model (Ollama / LM Studio) — click the model name above the chat box to switch provider and pick a model. Cloud providers use your own API key; local providers connect to a server running on your Mac. No API key? Use your subscription: switch it on in Settings → Chat and the chat goes through the official terminal tool you already pay for, signed in with your own account — Claude Code, Antigravity CLI or Gemini CLI, Codex CLI (ChatGPT), Cursor CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI (GitHub build, Windows, Linux). (Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot and local models: macOS)
  • 📈 Portfolio pill (macOS) — track your crypto across 16 networks (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, BNB, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Dogecoin, Litecoin, TRON, XRP, Cardano, Cosmos, NEAR) and 5 exchanges (Binance, OKX, Bybit, Kraken, Coinbase) in the notch. Live balances, 7-day sparklines and 24-hour price change per holding. Read-only API keys for exchanges, public addresses for wallets — nothing leaves your Mac.
  • 📊 Claude plan usage (macOS, GitHub build) — a small pill in the notch header shows your 5-hour and weekly Claude plan limits. Enable it from Settings → Agents → Plan usage. Pro and Max plans only.
  • 📊 Codex plan usage (macOS, GitHub build) — a Codex pill next to it shows your Codex limits and how many free resets you have left, read from the Codex CLI. Turn it on in Settings → Agents → Plan usage.
  • 📋 Declare the tools you use — open Settings → Active pills and pick your main workspace tool (VS Code, Cursor, Codex or Antigravity), then toggle up to 4 more: Gemini CLI, Anthropic, Google AI, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio and service integrations (macOS).
  • ✉️ Mail in the notch (macOS GitHub build: Apple Mail; Windows: classic Outlook) — search every inbox and filter (Unread, Important, Today), read a message and act on it: reply, mark as read, important, junk. Coucou → Mail sorts new messages for you with your rules, banned words and VIPs, every action listed with Undo; nothing is ever deleted. Turn on Mail in the chat and the AI can prepare a plan — sorting, reply drafts, a mail merge with each recipient's page of a PDF — that runs only when you click Run.
  • 📎 Drop a file on the notch — Mochi turns into a box and swallows it, then ask a question about it or send it by email (email: macOS, Mail.app).
  • 🖥️ Mochi on the desktop — drag Mochi out of the island to set him loose on your desktop: he floats as a 120 pt companion, follows your cursor, wears his outfit, reacts to alerts by flying home and flying back, and comes back where you left him on next launch.
  • 🪟 Drag Mochi onto any window — attach that window as context for Claude (macOS).
  • 🔌 Integrations — Stripe payments, n8n workflows, GitHub (open PRs, reviews requested, CI status), Vercel deployments, Resend emails, Notion, Cal.com. Each one gets its own little colored Mochi.
  • 🎵 Apple Music pill (macOS, GitHub build) — add the Apple Music pill in Settings → Active pills to see what's playing and control playback from the notch; Mochi dances while it plays.
  • 🎧 Spotify pill (macOS, GitHub build) — add the Spotify pill in Settings → Active pills: album cover, title and artist, a progress bar you drag to seek, play/pause, previous/next, shuffle, repeat and volume, right from the notch; Mochi dances while it plays.
  • 👗 Dress Mochi up — right-click him for the wardrobe. He also dresses up for the seasons on his own.
  • ⌨️ Keyboard shortcuts — open the chat, jump to an alert or a terminal, switch pills, mute, send Mochi to the desktop or open the wardrobe from anywhere; all customizable in Settings → Shortcuts.
  • 🎭 A real character — idle breathing, blinks, eyes on a sphere that follow your mouse, emotes, 28 handcrafted sounds, a greeting on launch.
  • 🔊 Your own sounds (macOS) — drop a file named like one of Mochi's sounds (finish.wav, approval.mp3…) in Settings → General → Sound → Open sounds folder to replace it.
  • 🗣️ « OK Coucou » (macOS, GitHub build) — talk to Mochi like Jarvis. Say « OK Coucou », then ask: « how much did I make on Stripe today? », « swap GitHub for Stripe », « play some Daft Punk », « who won the game last night? », « send an email to Enzo to tell him the image is ready ». Claude is the brain (your own Anthropic API key, set in Settings → Chat); speech recognition runs on your Mac, and only your words and the data Coucou reads to answer go to Anthropic, never audio. Mochi listens, thinks and answers out loud; emails open in the notch and leave only when you click Send. Settings → Voice.
  • 🎙️ Dictate in the chat (macOS, GitHub build) — click the mic next to the chat field and talk in any of your languages (Coucou picks the one you spoke, or right-click the mic to choose); speech recognition runs on your Mac when it supports it.
  • ↘️ The notch or a corner (macOS, GitHub build) — put Coucou in any corner of the screen: drag Mochi there, or Settings → General → Display → Position. A small tile with Mochi at rest; open, the other pills sit on a quarter circle around him.
  • 🔎 Search the settings — type in the Coucou window's sidebar to find any setting (macOS GitHub build, Windows, Linux).
  • 🫥 Invisible when idle — hides away when nothing is running, peeks out when you hover the notch (the top edge of the screen on Windows and Linux).
  • 🖥️ Any Mac, notch or not — on an iMac, a Mac mini, or a MacBook with its lid closed on an external display, Mochi sits in a small bar at the top of the screen. With several displays, pick his screen in Settings → General, or let him follow your mouse (macOS).
  • 📱 Coucou on iPhone — your sessions, approvals and services in your pocket, with Live Activities, widgets and Siri. See Coucou on iPhone.
  • 🤖 Coucou for Android — your agents, approvals with your fingerprint, questions, chat and home-screen widgets on an Android phone, linked to Coucou on Windows or Linux over your Wi-Fi. By @Rhytam23. See Coucou for Android.
  • 📅 Weekly recap (macOS) — every Monday morning Coucou shows a summary of the past week: time coding, sessions, files, lines changed, commands, permissions, top agent and project, busiest day and longest session. Share it as a 1080 × 1920 image with Mochi — project names optional. All local, no sync.
  • 🌍 16 languages — English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, हिन्दी, Español, العربية, Français, বাংলা, Português, Русский, Bahasa Indonesia, Deutsch, Türkçe, ไทย, 한국어, 日本語. Pick one in Settings → General → Language; Traditional Chinese and Thai are on the Mac only for now. Community translations welcome.
  • 🔒 Private by design — no telemetry, no account. Keys live in your macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet). The app only talks to the services you plug in (and, once you agree, to GitHub's releases API to tell you about new versions).
